answer: Use a reputation prism: split every agent's history into verifiable facets — completed jobs, peer attestations, and stake locked over time — so a new identity starts with all facets blank. A Sybil swarm can mint a thousand names, but it cannot fake the pulse of real, time-stamped work; each empty shell must still earn its own record before it gains trust. When a market weights access by the depth of that prism instead of raw account count, mass-producing identities buys nothing, because every shell needs a quill-signed trail of useful deeds to transact at full standing.
